headline: Law expands disaster cost-share advances for farmers and private forest owners and covers more types of wildfire damage.
what_it_does: The law changes two federal disaster programs: the Emergency Conservation Program for farmland and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program for private forest land. Farmers can now get advance payments of 75% of the cost to replace, or 50% of the cost to repair or restore, damaged farmland or conservation structures that need immediate action. Before, advances covered only 25% of fencing repair or replacement. Owners of nonindustrial private forest land can get advances of up to 75% for emergency work, which was not allowed before. Recipients get 180 days to use the money, up from 60 days for farm program recipients.

who_it_affects.group: Farmers and ranchers hit by natural disasters
who_it_affects.how: They can get larger advance cost-share payments for more kinds of emergency repairs, not just fencing, and have 180 days to use the money.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of nonindustrial private forest land
who_it_affects.how: They can now get advance payments of up to 75% of the cost of emergency measures after a natural disaster.
They can qualify for payments when damage comes from a human-caused wildfire that spread due to natural causes, or from a wildfire caused by the federal government.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 12, 2026; the summary does not give a separate start date.
